model: UK online men's health clinic and pharmacy: an anonymous questionnaire, then the patient picks a subscription product, pays upfront for 3, 6 or 12 months, and a clinician reviews the request after checkout.

access.accountWall: At …/subscribe/hair-loss/<draft id>/profile, after the questionnaire, GP choice, optional email (skippable), product selection, 'what to expect', billing frequency and add-ons. The screen shows the order summary and asks for email, password, legal name, date of birth, phone, sex and delivery address. The full recommendation and all plan prices are visible before it. Direct purchase of Rosemary Oil hits the same form on its first screen.
access.coverageNote: Stage 1 mapped all 29 questions and every option's served result. Stage 2 (23 Nov 2026) replayed the baseline to the account wall and ran 32 one-change replays to the product screen (runs/x2-*), covering every option that the served data or stage 1 suggested could change the offer: both allergies, lactose, each scalp symptom alone, every caution and its opt-out, the whole mental-health branch, three stops, a stop-bypass, age 65+, three patterns, two preference answers, medical history and two entry links with an allergy. Nothing after the account wall was tried. No contact details were entered anywhere. Stage 3 (24 Nov 2026) replayed the baseline twice (to the product screen and to the account wall), re-tested ten stage-2 rules and ran the main untested options (Complete, 65+ No, Temples, Moderate, asthma and baby opt-ins, lactose small, All of the above, the minoxidil entry link, a two-rule pair with and without an entry link, and the Finasteride billing screen): 22 replays in runs/verify-*.

flows.name: Men's hair-loss consultation (questionnaire 'hair_loss', version 14, revision 'smart')
flows.stagesSummary: Consent screen → 8 to 28 anonymous questions out of a bank of 29 (the baseline man sees 8) → GP-notification choice → optional email (skippable) → product selection (the recommendation) → 'what to expect' → billing frequency → add-ons → ACCOUNT WALL at …/profile (order summary + create account + address) → payment, identity check and clinician review (not tested).

questions.text: The really important bit. By clicking “Next”, you are confirming that you: Are completing this consultation for yourself and to the best of your knowledge. Were assigned male at birth. Will disclose any serious illnesses or operations you have had or any prescription medication you currently take. Will only use one method of hair loss treatment at a time and will not combine more than one different medication for the condition. Are aware that finasteride is associated with depression, suicidal thoughts, and sexual dysfunction including decreased sex drive, erectile dysfunction, and ejaculation problems. These side effects can occur independently of each other and may persist after stopping treatment. A clinician will review your suitability before any prescription is issued. Will answer the questions in the next section about your physical and mental health history honestly, and are aware that your responses are reviewed by a prescribing clinician and kept confidential. Are aware that you should not take finasteride if you’re trying for a baby. Are aware that you may be prescribed an unlicensed treatment. Are accepting our Terms & Conditions and Terms of Sale.

options.label: Next
options.effect: Creates an anonymous draft on Numan's server (POST api.numan.com/v1/subscriptions, status 'draft', questionnaire hair_loss version 14, revision 'smart') and opens the first question. Sex is never asked as a question: being assigned male at birth is asserted here.

questions.purpose: Consent, declaration of male sex at birth, finasteride risk warnings and notice that an unlicensed medicine may be prescribed.
questions.shownWhen: always (entry screen of every hair-loss consultation link)

questions.text: Please tell us your age.

options.label: 65 or over
options.effect: Adds one confirmation question. If he says Yes, the offer is the same as the baseline (nothing hidden although the API variants say up to 65). Run x2-22.
Goes on to the hair-loss pattern question.

options.label: Under 18
options.effect: Hard stop: 'No suitable treatment', see your doctor or email the clinic. Soft in practice: 'Review your answers' lets him change it.

questions.purpose: Age gate. Under-18s are refused; 65 and over get an extra confirmation.
questions.branchDetail: Under 18 stops; 65 or over adds one question.

questions.text: Hair loss products are not guaranteed to show results in individuals over the age of 65, however, there is still a possibility for hair growth to reoccur. Would you still like to be considered for treatments?

options.label: Yes
options.effect: Continues. No change to the offer (all eight products, three-part kit featured). Run x2-22.

options.label: No
options.effect: Stops: 'No suitable treatment. Unfortunately, we’re unable to recommend a hair loss treatment for you. Please contact your doctor for advice.' with the clinic email and 'Review your answers'. Run verify-12-age-65-no.

questions.purpose: Sets expectations for older men and lets them opt out.
questions.branchDetail: No stops the consultation.

questions.text: What kind of hair loss do you have?

options.label: Temples
options.effect: Continues; no extra question and no change to the offer (three-part kit featured, all eight products). Run verify-19-pat-temples.

options.label: Temples and Crown
options.effect: Proceeds to the onset question. Baseline answer.

options.label: Moderate
options.effect: Continues; no extra question and no change to the offer (three-part kit featured, all eight products). Run verify-20-pat-moderate.

options.label: Extensive
options.effect: Continues; no extra question. No change to the offer (all eight products, three-part kit featured). Run x2-29.

options.label: Patchy
options.effect: Stop screen: circular patches may be alopecia areata, see your GP (x2-26). 'Review your answers' goes back and a different answer continues in the same draft (x2-32).

options.label: Complete
options.effect: Stops at once: 'No suitable treatment. Our treatments are not effective in individuals who have experienced complete hair loss.' with the clinic email and a 'Review your answers' button. Run verify-11-pat-complete.

options.label: Other hair loss pattern
options.effect: Adds a free-text description and a clinician note. No change to the offer (all eight products, three-part kit featured). Run x2-24.

questions.purpose: Picture-based pattern check (seven drawings) to confirm male pattern hair loss and screen out patchy or complete loss.
questions.branchDetail: Patchy and Complete stop; Other adds a text box; the other four change nothing (x2-24, x2-26, x2-29).

questions.text: Please tell us about your hair loss: can you describe the appearance of your hair loss; do you have a diagnosis for your hair loss?; for how long has it occurred?; has anything made it better or worse, such as stress?; do you have any other symptoms?. This information is needed so that our clinicians can ensure the prescription is safe for you to take.
questions.purpose: Free-text description for the clinician when the pattern does not match the drawings.

questions.text: When did you start to notice your hair loss?

options.label: Over the last few days or weeks
options.effect: Stop screen: not designed for sudden hair loss, see your GP (x2-25).

options.label: My hair loss started gradually over the last few months or years
options.effect: Proceeds to the allergy question.

questions.purpose: Screens out sudden hair loss, which needs a GP.
questions.branchDetail: Sudden onset stops the consultation.

questions.text: Do you have an allergy or intolerance to any of the following?

options.label: I am allergic to minoxidil
options.effect: Adds a reaction text box; sets hasAllergyToMinoxidil. Removes the minoxidil group hidden (all kits, both sprays, Regaine); Finasteride featured 'Recommended for you' £16.80, Rosemary Oil also listed. Run x2-03. Exception: the product named in the entry link stays (x2-20).

options.label: I am allergic to finasteride
options.effect: Adds a reaction text box; sets hasAllergyToFinasteride. Removes the finasteride group hidden (all kits, Triple-Action Spray, Finasteride); Extra Strength Spray featured 'Recommended for you' £18.00, Regaine and Rosemary Oil also listed. Run x2-02. Exception: the entry product stays (x2-21).

options.label: I have a lactose intolerance or allergy
options.effect: Adds the lactose tolerance question. Nothing is hidden, even with 'can't tolerate any'. Run x2-18.

options.label: I am not allergic to any of the above
options.effect: Exclusive option. Proceeds to the scalp question.

questions.purpose: Drug allergy and lactose screen. This is the main automatic product filter.
questions.branchDetail: Each drug allergy removes that drug's whole product group (x2-02, x2-03) except an entry-link product (x2-20, x2-21). Lactose adds a question but removes nothing (x2-18).

questions.text: Please let us know how you react when you take this medicine
questions.purpose: Free-text description of the allergic reaction for the clinician.
questions.shownWhen: minoxidil and/or finasteride allergy ticked (seen with each alone: x2-02, x2-03)

questions.text: Finasteride tablets contain very small amounts of lactose. If you have taken a tablet formulation before without experiencing symptoms, it is unlikely that you will get undesirable effects from the lactose within our tablets.

options.label: I can’t tolerate any amount of lactose and I would like to be considered for non-lactose containing preparations only
options.effect: Clinician note only ('confirm the request is for a lactose-free treatment'); finasteride tablets stay on offer. Run x2-18.

options.label: I can tolerate very small amounts of lactose
options.effect: Continues. Flags unchanged apart from the allergy list (lactose_intolerance_or_allergy); offer identical to baseline. Run verify-17-al-lac-small.

questions.purpose: Checks whether trace lactose in finasteride tablets is acceptable.

questions.text: Are you experiencing any of the following symptoms on your scalp?

options.label: Pain, itching, burning or bumps
options.effect: Adds a text box and sets isMinoxidilEligible=false: minoxidil group hidden (all kits, both sprays, Regaine); Finasteride featured 'Recommended for you' £16.80, Rosemary Oil also listed. Run x2-04.

options.label: Red rinds or rashes
options.effect: Adds a text box and sets isMinoxidilEligible=false: minoxidil group hidden (all kits, both sprays, Regaine); Finasteride featured 'Recommended for you' £16.80, Rosemary Oil also listed. Run x2-05.

options.label: Dandruff
options.effect: Adds the 'still consider topical?' question. Nothing hidden whatever the answer (x2-06, x2-07).

options.label: Psoriasis or eczema
options.effect: Adds a text box and a clinician note saying minoxidil is not suitable. Minoxidil is NOT hidden: No change to the offer (all eight products, three-part kit featured). Run x2-08.

options.label: No
options.effect: Exclusive option. Proceeds to 'Are any of the following true?'.

questions.purpose: Scalp-condition screen; active scalp disease is a reason not to use minoxidil.
questions.branchDetail: Pain/itching and red rinds/rashes each remove all minoxidil products (x2-04, x2-05). Dandruff and psoriasis/eczema add a follow-up but remove nothing (x2-06..08). Each symptom adds its own follow-up.

questions.text: You mentioned you have pain, itching, burning or bumps on your scalp. Have they been seen to or treated by a doctor?; If so, what treatments have you received?; Please give us a detailed description of your scalp condition below (including how long you’ve had it, its appearance and any other symptoms it is causing)
questions.purpose: Free-text detail about scalp pain, itching, burning or bumps for the clinician.
questions.shownWhen: scalp: 'Pain, itching, burning or bumps' ticked

questions.text: You mentioned you have red rinds or rashes on your scalp. Have they been seen to or treated by a doctor?; If so, what treatments have you received?; Please give us a detailed description of your scalp condition below (including how long you’ve had it, its appearance and any other symptoms it is causing).
questions.purpose: Free-text detail about red rinds or rashes for the clinician.

questions.text: Topical formulations (such as spray) may worsen dandruff. Would you still like to be considered for topical treatments?

options.label: Yes
options.effect: No change to the offer (all eight products, three-part kit featured). Run x2-06.

options.label: No
options.effect: Clinician note only ('confirm request is not topical'). Sprays stay on offer. Run x2-07.

questions.branchDetail: Neither answer changes the offer (x2-06, x2-07); 'No' adds a clinician note.

questions.text: You mentioned you have eczema or psoriasis on your scalp. Have they been seen to or treated by a doctor?; If so, what treatments have you received?; Please give us a detailed description of your scalp condition below (including how long you’ve had it, its appearance and any other symptoms it is causing)
questions.purpose: Free-text detail about scalp psoriasis or eczema for the clinician.

questions.text: Are any of the following true?

options.label: I have noticed hair loss on other areas of my body other than my head.
options.effect: Adds a text box and a clinician note. No change to the offer (all eight products, three-part kit featured). Run x2-19.

options.label: I am undergoing PSA (prostate) monitoring or I have previously been diagnosed with prostate cancer.
options.effect: Adds the PSA follow-up. Neither follow-up answer hides anything (x2-09, x2-31).

options.label: I have been diagnosed with high or low blood pressure.
options.effect: Adds the blood-pressure follow-up and sets isMinoxidilEligible=false whatever the follow-up answer: minoxidil group hidden (all kits, both sprays, Regaine); Finasteride featured 'Recommended for you' £16.80, Rosemary Oil also listed. Runs x2-10, x2-30.

options.label: I have been diagnosed with asthma.
options.effect: Adds the asthma follow-up. Neither answer hides the sprays (x2-11).

options.label: I plan on trying for a baby in the next 12 weeks.
options.effect: Adds the fertility follow-up. Neither answer hides finasteride (x2-12).

options.label: I have previously experienced, or am currently experiencing, depression, anxiety or panic disorders
options.effect: Starts the mental-health branch (mood risk, then who manages it, medicines, dose change, suicidal thoughts). With all neutral answers the offer is unchanged (x2-14).

options.label: No - none
options.effect: Exclusive option. Skips all eleven follow-ups and goes to the 'most important' question.

questions.purpose: One screen for six cautions: body hair loss, prostate monitoring or cancer, blood pressure, asthma, trying for a baby, mental health.
questions.branchDetail: Blood pressure removes all minoxidil products whatever the follow-up (x2-10, x2-30). Depression opens the mental-health branch, which can remove finasteride. PSA, asthma, baby and body hair add a follow-up but remove nothing (x2-09, x2-11, x2-12, x2-19).

questions.text: Please tell us about hair loss in areas other than your head. This information is needed so that our clinicians can ensure the prescription is safe for you to take.

questions.text: If you wish to be considered for finasteride you must tell your GP that you are taking finasteride so that they can interpret your results accordingly.

options.effect: No change to the offer (all eight products, three-part kit featured). Run x2-31.

options.label: I do not wish to be considered for finasteride containing preparations.

options.label: I understand that minoxidil may lower my blood pressure and would like to be considered for minoxidil.
options.effect: Minoxidil is still removed (the removal comes from ticking blood pressure): minoxidil group hidden (all kits, both sprays, Regaine); Finasteride featured 'Recommended for you' £16.80, Rosemary Oil also listed. Run x2-30.

options.label: I do not wish to be considered for minoxidil.

engineSummary: Numan's engine is simple. The server serves one question at a time and a few answers stop the consultation (under 18, patchy or complete loss, sudden onset, 65+ saying No), but every stop has a 'Review your answers' button that lets the patient change the answer and carry on. After each answer the server works out two yes/no flags, finasteride allowed and minoxidil allowed, plus an allergy list. The product screen hides every product containing a drug that is not allowed and features one product: the three-part kit by default, the product in the entry link if there was one (even when its drug is ruled out), or the first product left (Finasteride or Extra Strength Spray). Live tests show only seven answers move a flag: either drug allergy, scalp pain/itching, red rinds/rashes, any blood-pressure diagnosis (minoxidil off), and 'minoxidil only', specialist-managed mental health or recent suicidal thoughts (finasteride off). Everything else, including psoriasis/eczema and the patient's own 'I do not wish to be considered' answers for prostate monitoring, asthma and trying for a baby, changes nothing on screen: it only becomes a note for the clinician who reviews the order after payment details are taken. Pattern, age over 65 and preferences never change the offer. There is no dose or strength choice in the quiz: each product has one strength.
strengths: Fast and low friction: 8 questions for a straightforward man, the full offer and every price before any sign-in.
A clear, tested safety filter for the two drugs: allergies, scalp inflammation and blood pressure remove minoxidil, and mood risk removes finasteride, on screen and before checkout (x2 runs).
Targeted follow-ups: each caution opens its own short explanation and choice instead of a long form; specialist-managed patients skip irrelevant questions.
Detailed written clinician instructions sit behind every risky answer (in the served data), so the human review has a playbook.
Always leaves something to buy (Rosemary Oil), and the money-back guarantee and kit discounts are visible throughout.
weaknesses: Patient opt-outs are ignored on screen: 'I do not wish to be considered for finasteride' (prostate monitoring, trying for a baby) and 'not topical' (asthma, dandruff) leave those products on offer and the finasteride kit featured (x2-09, x2-11, x2-12, x2-07).

Psoriasis/eczema on the scalp does not remove minoxidil, although Numan's own clinician note says minoxidil is not suitable with an active scalp condition (x2-08); pain/itching and red rinds do remove it.

Product links bypass the safety filter: the entry product stays featured even with an allergy to its drug (x2-20, x2-21, verify-08) or when its drug is ruled out by a scalp answer (verify-21: Regaine offered with scalp pain and a finasteride allergy).
Stops are soft: 'Review your answers' lets anyone change a stopping answer and continue in the same draft (x2-32).

Suicidal thoughts in the past year give no stop or signposting screen; the man is simply moved to minoxidil products (x2-16). A recent mental-health dose change skips the suicidal-thoughts question altogether (x2-17).
Ticking blood pressure removes minoxidil even when the man says he understands and wants it (x2-30): blunt for well-controlled hypertension on topical minoxidil (our clinical view, inferred).

Thin history: no exact age, duration, family history, previous treatments or side effects, sexual side-effect history, or treatment preference (tablet vs topical); lactose 'none' does not remove the tablets (x2-18).
Men only: no women's consultation at all; the only consultation requires 'assigned male at birth'.
opportunities: Serve women: a female pattern hair-loss consultation (topical and oral minoxidil, spironolactone pathways) is entirely missing at Numan.
Honour patient choices at once: if someone opts out of a drug or a form, show only what they asked for, and explain why.

Offer strength and form choices (oral minoxidil, several minoxidil strengths, topical finasteride on its own). Numan has topical finasteride only inside its combination spray, and its quiz never asks about strength or form.
Collect a fuller history (duration, family history, previous treatment and side effects, sexual function, photos) and use it to personalise and to set expectations.
Stronger mental-health safety: a crisis signposting screen for recent suicidal thoughts and asking it regardless of dose changes.
Close the entry-link gap and lock stop screens for the session, then advertise the stricter safety as a trust point.

verification.verdict: Trustworthy as labelled. Every high-consequence rule I re-tested (ten of them, plus both baselines) gave exactly the recorded result, and the live catalogue and product pages match the recorded names, strengths and prices. I found no contradicted rule. The errors I found were small: two stops and one pair rule rested on code or a mixed walk (now observed), one opportunity wrongly said Numan has no topical finasteride, and one clinical opinion was not labelled. The new finding is that product entry links beat the eligibility flags as well as the allergy flags. The main limit is structural: the engine's flags are computed on Numan's server and everything after the account wall, including the clinician's final decision, is unseen, so the report describes what the anonymous quiz offers, not what is finally prescribed.
